heuristics: H1: the class-level r-adding walk with 2^16 adders behaves as a random mapping on the (r-1)/6 order-6 classes, up to an exponent penalty of at most 4/2^16. Used only for the collision statistics of section 7.

M1 (replaces the fresh-class premise H2; the only premise besides H1 and H3): every class-level value the walk reads (the class key, which fixes the adder index, the filter bits and the DP test; the canonical rotation k; the canonical sign s; and the coordinate fraction values of the canonical representative used by the exact-k test) is a function of the class alone, and the values of distinct classes are independent and uniform, independent of x. Derivation (proof.md sections 3 to 6): closure rates are exact algebra under M1 (2-cycles 1/(6A); 3..64-cycles at most 0.1/A^2, with 3/A^2 kept as the bound); within-trail coincidences use Lemma G, which needs only independence of distinct classes; the abandonment bound (Lemma T') is a first-moment bound over closures and needs only the per-step closure bound; the rare-work rates (Lemma M') follow from the same per-step bounds for every processed step, revisits included, and the exact-k fallback rate 2^-55 per canon call follows from the uniformity of the fraction values (the fallback window has width 2^-55.7 for uniform fractions). No freshness of escape points or independence across trails is assumed beyond M1.

H3: Callgrind instruction counts on production inputs represent the common path: 808.67 (plain) and 818.66 (anchor) instructions per walk step, plus at most 2 for the canon_pick branch (C_COMMON = 821), with the rare paths out of line and charged at worst case; the Markov reserve covers the expected rare work.
limitations: The model success bound is 0.411524 at tau = 0.5303, 0.0215 above 0.39; pooled toy-curve success at that budget is in the evidence.
Analytic production cost; no production-size execution.
Needs about 2^67.7 stored distinguished points; not a practical attack.
All field arithmetic is the package's own inline assembly, tested against Python big integers but not formally verified.

H1 and M1 are unproved heuristics. The algorithm's own randomness (the table and every trail's coins) is drawn from the operating system and is not a heuristic (proof.md section 2.2). The argument is not established at production size: the toy runs use theta = 2^-5, and the formal test (evidence/formal-structure.json) uses 6 adder bits and theta = 2^-6, so neither tests M1 at production theta or adder count.
Escape depths of 2^50 or more are covered only by the depth tail (proof.md section 2.3), a first-moment bound under M1. The certificate of section 2.4 is exact for depths below 2^50.
The exact certificate of section 2.4 (no k < 2^50 with 2^k in Gamma, from baby-step giant-step over the secp256k1 order) is exact and needs no assumption.
Distinguished points never occur in a production-parameter measurement sample; the restart and abandonment paths were checked on small builds.

The rare-path charges are forced-path maxima measured with a bounding build (proof.md section 8.1); the bounding build is checked for equality and for dominance on the forced paths, not proved for every input.

The exact-k fallback rate (2^-55 per canon call, proof.md section 6) follows from M1 extended to the canonical coordinate fractions, and is not measured: no fallback occurred in the measured steps, which does not test that rate.
The work meter's abort probability, 1/64, is a Markov bound on the expected metered rare work under M1 (Lemma M'), and is counted in delta.

The measurement harness takes restart starts from a precomputed pool of 1024 points (measurement/step.c, new_trail), so restarts there reuse starts; the specified algorithm draws fresh coins for every restart and is charged at its cost (proof.md section 2.5). The kernel was not changed.

The replay cut-off (65n steps, REPLAY_FACTOR = 65) is in the core and the regenerated experiment.py, and a cut-off replay fails the run, counted in DELTA_CUT (proof.md sections 1.3 and 3). The kernel and the replica do not replay and were not changed; the small builds were not rerun for the cut-off.
